 Order

This is first application filed by the applicant under section 438 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail relating to FIR No. 935 of 2023 registered at Police Station - Cantt., District- Guna (M.P.) for offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 of I.P.C.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.

It is further argued that entire prosecution story is highly improbable because the registered power of attorney was executed on 13.09.1988 and on the basis of that power of attorney, on 14.09.1988, brother of the complainant Zameel Khan, executed a sale-deed in favour of the applicant.

Further argument is that on 14.6.2003, registered sale deed was again executed by Zameel Khan in favour of Abdul, thereafter, on 24.8.2005, present applicant executed a sale deed in Abdul Naeem Qureshi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43015353/

sentences.text: 1 favour of Afroza, however, complainant never challenged aforementioned transaction before any competent civil court.

In the light of the fact that power of attorney was never challenged before civil court and not declared as forged, prima facie, ingredients of Sections 420, 467, 468 and 471 of IPC do not attract against the applicant.
Learned counsel for the applicant further argued that present case is of civil nature and wrongly been given colour of criminal case.
Applicant is aged about 64 years having no criminal antecedents.
He is the permanent resident of District Guna (M.P.) and there is no possibility of his absconsion or tampering with the prosecution evidence.

Co-accused Smt. Afroj Kureshi has already been granted anticipatory bail by this Court by order dated 09.1.2024 passed in MCRC No.57748 of 2023 and case of the present applicant is on same footing as of co-accused.
Applicant is ready and willing to co-operate in the investigation and shall abide by all the terms and conditions as may be imposed by this Court; therefore, he prays for grant of anticipatory bail.
O n the other hand, learned State counsel as well as counsel for the complainant have vehemently opposed the application and prays for its rejection.
Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the case diary available on record.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed and it is directed that in the event of arrest, the applicant be released on bail, on executing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/-(Rupees One Lac Only)
with two solvent sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer/Investigating Authority.

The applicant shall further abide by other conditions enumerated under Section 438 (2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure and shall cooperate in the investigation, otherwise this bail order shall automatically stand cancelled.
Certified copy as per rules.

(SUNITA YADAV) JUDGE AKS Abdul Naeem Qureshi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43015353/
